Sometimes, however, you just want an overexcited announcer to shout “Awesome!” while you sail a Jeep Gladiator over a crest, misjudge the landing, and impact an immovable sandstone massif at 85 mph.

Such is the appeal of Moab Run , a new retro-themed off-roading game from none other than Jeep itself. Playable on mobile or in a browser window, the game channels the best of 1990s-era 3-D games like Sega Rally or Offroad Challenge , infusing it with playable examples of the very real special-edition Wranglers Jeep has launched over the past year or so.

The in-demand Neue Klasse cars have consistently outperformed in real-world range tests, and last year BMW drove an iX3 from Debrecen, Hungary, to Munich, Germany, covering 626 miles on a single charge .

To show off just how road-trip-capable its Neue Klasse cars are, BMW took the new i3 on the Paneuropeana, a long-distance EV rally route devised by Rafael de Mestre, who has circumnavigated the globe in electric cars four times. The car covered 5,886.7 kilometers on the journey, or 3,658 miles rounded up — over 1,000 miles more than you'd drive when crossing the United States. It took 3 days, 2 hours and 41 minutes to complete the drive, and only 2 hours and 46 minutes was spent charging. Is that fast enough for you, yet?

Jaguar Land Rover has suffered a setback in its dispute with BYD over the Ti 7 SUV. In a preliminary ruling on 11 November 2026, the District Court of The Hague lifted an August evidence seizure and directed JLR to instruct the court-appointed custodian to destroy the seized records. JLR has 24 hours from formal service of the ruling to issue those instructions. A delay could trigger a penalty of Euro 50,000 (Rs 52 lakh) per hour, capped at Euro 500,000 (Rs 5.2 crore).

Court-appointed bailiffs seized records from BYD’s offices in Schiedam and Hoofddorp in August after JLR obtained authorisation from a Dutch court. JLR alleges that the Ti 7 copies elements of the Land Rover Defender’s design and suspects that BYD dismantled a Defender to reverse-engineer parts of the vehicle.

Unless you only travel within driving distance of home or are willing to spend the time and money on shipping , we will all end up in a situation where renting a car is a necessity. There may be plenty of cities with fantastic public transportation systems, but you just need a car to venture out and explore the countryside. Many of us are far more care-free behind the wheel when the vehicle is owned by an abstract corporate entity and not a person with a face.

What's the worst way you've abused a rental car? I'm not talking about returning it with an empty tank. That's just a surcharge that rental companies are more than happy to add to your bill. Abuse is real, lasting damage that's an absolute nightmare to reverse. Let me use a hypothetical beach day in the South of France as an example. You and a few friends take a decent Peugeot 408 to a sleepy village on the Mediterranean. After a fun day of sand and surf, everyone piles back into the sedan right off the beach, covering the interior with sand. That's the appetizer. On the drive back, you get impatient sitting behind a truck on a two-lane road. You pull into the oncoming lane but don't get entirely clear, and you sideswipe the truck. The 408 is far worse off, with its entire right side scratched up. That's abuse!

The current Honda CR-V can be had with or without a hybrid powertrain. However, when the compact SUV’s newest generation arrives sometime next year, it’ll only be available as a hybrid. Honda’s announcement comes a year after Toyota applied the same strategy with its new RAV4 . And considering over half the CR-Vs Honda sells are hybrids, the move makes a lot of sense.

Apart from introducing a standard hybrid powertrain, the 2028 Honda CR-V will mark the start of the bestselling nameplate’s seventh generation. The South Delhi District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has directed Eicher Motors and Noida-based Shree Mahadev Motors to jointly pay Rs 1 lakh to a Royal Enfield Interceptor 650 owner. The order, dated 4 November 2026, concerns a September 2021 trip to Leh during which the rider said his motorcycle repeatedly lost power . The commission found no email on record showing that corrective work had been carried out on his bike.

The complainant, Hasan Murtaza, bought the Interceptor 650 from Ess Aar Motors on 13 April 2019. Before setting out for Leh, he took the motorcycle to Shree Mahadev Motors in June 2021. According to his complaint, he told the service centre about the planned trip and specifically asked it to update the electronic control unit (ECU) to address reports of power loss at high altitude. He said the workshop told him the update had been installed and the bike was ready for the trip.

SpaceX filed its intention to build a new AI data center at its facility in Starbase, Texas, which will be powered by a new natural gas plant that it will also build. None of that sounds like space, but this is the company that SpaceX has become. The initial phase of this build-out is projected to cost $24 billion, though more phases are to come. Critically, this gives the rocket company, which is also an internet company, which is also an AI company, which is also a social media company, a way to make use of its newest product: natural gas. Again, space!

The company has been moving towards an expansion into fossil fuels for the last few months. In June, SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell said the company was making plans for "basically mining our own natural gas... to develop our own propellant and bring it to the rocket." The rocket in question being Starship, which SpaceX is essentially betting its future on . That takes a mixture of methane and liquid oxygen to fire up its thrusters; methane can be extracted from natural gas. For that reason, the company has made major moves to ensure its own supply. It hired for its own natural gas trader, normally an oil industry job for buying and selling the stuff, and is building its own pipelines in both Florida and Texas, per Bloomberg .

No, unfortunately for everyone who still has to work for a living, Kelley Blue Book reports the average transaction price for new cars hasn't just crossed the $50,000 mark. In October, the average transaction price rose to a level never before seen in the U.S. So that's pretty exciting. Aren't you thrilled to be alive right now to experience it?

Using data from its parent company, Cox Automotive, KBB says the average price consumers paid for new cars in the U.S. hit $51,109 in the month of October. That's 1.3% higher than it was in September and a 2.1% increase year-over-year. Higher prices aren't usually a good thing, especially when those higher prices are on things most people need to use every day (cars) instead of luxuries that you don't have to own to participate in society. The average MSRP of new vehicles is also up, reportedly hitting $52,933 in October, up 1.4% versus September and 2.4% higher year-over-year.
